properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony thinking out loud, 2026-08-20. Nothing here is intent and nothing should be built against it without his word.

HIS WORDS: "line up the work we're doing in increments/epochs (this already can be done, but this should become more like the default when user of reflow2 lines up a set of tasks)."

WHAT IS ALREADY TRUE, so the idea is about REACH rather than about capability: plan_epoch, add_release, schedule_for and arrival_delta all exist and work. The plan-increments skill describes the whole discipline including the four conventions nobody guesses. So this is not a missing mechanism. It is a mechanism that only fires when somebody remembers it exists.

THE SHAPE OF THE IDEA: today a user who lists five things to do gets five things done. The list lives in the conversation, or in a commit message, or in the agent's head. The plan-increments skill already names this exact failure in as many words — "if you are maintaining a numbered list of upcoming work in the conversation, that is a delivery plan living outside the graph" — and asks the agent to notice. Anthony's idea is that noticing should not be the mechanism.

WHY IT IS THE SAME PATTERN AS THREE THINGS FOUND THIS SESSION, which is the argument FOR it: the mechanism EXISTS, is TESTED, and is UNREACHABLE FROM WHERE THE PERSON IS STUCK. A user lining up tasks is exactly where an increment is owed, and nothing at that moment says so.

OPTIONS, none chosen:
  (a) A TOOL-LEVEL NUDGE, the pattern reflow2 already uses — the capture tools return loop_hint lines, and the same could fire when several capabilities or requirements are created in one batch with none scheduled. Cheap, consistent with dec:the-discipline-arrives-at-the-tool, and it is a HINT rather than a gate.
  (b) A DETECTOR — make 'work exists and is scheduled nowhere' a gap. The plan-increments skill already names unreleased_component as its gap, so half of this exists. Costs: on a young design almost everything is unscheduled, so it would fire everywhere and be trained away.
  (c) A DEFAULT INCREMENT — a project always has a current open epoch, and newly captured work lands in it unless told otherwise. Strongest reach. RISK, and it is the serious one: this asserts a plan the user never made, which is the opposite of every other default in reflow2 (req:defaults-do-not-assert). An increment nobody scoped is the thing arrival_delta already refuses to call ready to cut.
  (d) SKILL-LEVEL ONLY — sharpen the trigger wording and accept that it depends on the agent noticing. This is the status quo and it is what he is saying is not enough.

HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENT, recorded beside the idea rather than used to argue it down: reflow2's own increments have been planned by hand all session and it worked well — but only because the discipline was deliberately invoked. That is evidence for the idea, not against it. The real counter is (c)'s risk: a default that MAKES a plan is not the same as a default that ASKS for one, and only the second is in keeping with how reflow2 treats every other unstated thing.

RELATED AND SEPARATELY ANSWERABLE: dec:idea-an-increment-can-be-sliced-into-work-packages-with-an-owner and dec:idea-a-gap-can-be-scheduled-into-an-increment-like-any-other-work.
properties.name: OPEN — should lining work up in increments be the DEFAULT when a user lines up a set of tasks, rather than a skill someone remembers to reach for?
